open_requirements.requirement: Discord bot with rec commands, per-fandom feeds, account linking
open_requirements.notes: Gaps review E5. Extends §37 companion bot. | UNBLOCKED 2026-11-11 (credential supplied; token stored on the host only, never in the tree — [REDACTED] here). SCOPE DECISION: the spec's separate workspace with Poise+Serenity+Redis is rejected for this deployment — no Redis in the stack, a gateway websocket is a new always-on failure mode, and a separate workspace is invisible to gate.sh. It ships as an INTERACTIONS ENDPOINT on the existing server (Discord POSTs signed interactions; Ed25519 verified BEFORE parsing), so dispatch is an Axum handler the existing gates cover. Seven steps with acceptance tests are in docs/plans/roadmap-remaining.md; step 2 (signature before parse) and the /users/@me live proof come first. | CENSUS 2026-11-11 superseded my own plan: a darkhold bot ALREADY EXISTS (code-local/rust/darkbot, 12.5k lines, darkbot-adapter trait + conformance suite + discord/matrix/telegram). The interactions endpoint I wrote this turn was deleted — it was the third hand-rolled copy (ascend 818, darkhold 223, suki 170) of a ~120-line kit (leverage 9 = 3x3/1: not worth a crate). darkbot already calls darkhold's real API (public/search, public/works, works/{}/kudos, me/tokens, me/tokens/{}) which all exist. Its link handshake (bot/link/start + bot/link/exchange) contradicts §23.2, which is implemented and better: /me/bots/{id}/link-challenge -> GET /bots/link/{code} (reader sees what is asked) -> POST /bots/link/{code} (confirm; token issued once to the reader's session). darkbot adapts, not the server. REMAINING: point darkbot at live darkhold, adapt its two link calls, prove one command in a real guild. The shareable component is darkbot-adapter's PlatformMessage IR + Adapter trait + conformance (the second implementation is fanfic-archivist-bot's archivist-core, 30.7k lines) — converge only when a second non-darkhold bot needs it. | LINK CARDINALITY FIXED 2026-11-11 (M45-59): §23.2's confirmation used to rotate the registration's credential, making the bot single-reader — the second person to link revoked the first one's token and bot_for_token could not see links at all. Links are now per (bot, pseud) and suspension reaches them. REMAINING on this row is the credential half only: (1) a Discord APPLICATION for darkhold (the host holds only ~/.config/ascend-bot.env, which is ascend's identity — reusing it would post darkbot's replies as ascend), its token in ~/.config/darkbot-bot.env 0600, never in the tree; (2) DARKBOT_DARKHOLD_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8081/api/v1 plus DARKBOT_STORE_KEY (32 bytes hex); (3) the bot invited to a guild and one command proved live; (4) darkbot's two invented calls (bot/link/start, bot/link/exchange) replaced by GET /bots/link/{code} describe + the reader-confirms-on-the-site model. | CENSUS 2026-11-12 (step 4, the code half, measured before writing any): the two calls darkbot invents cannot simply be redirected, because darkhold's §23.2 flow is OWNER-INITIATED, not bot-initiated. `POST /me/bots/{id}/link-challenge` takes `RequireSession` — the bot's OWNER mints a code in a browser — and `GET/POST /bots/link/{code}` is the reader confirming on the site. That works for 'my bot, my account' and cannot work for a guild bot that must start the flow FOR a reader inside Discord: the bot has a bearer credential, not a session, so it cannot mint a code at all. That asymmetry is the reason darkbot grew `bot/link/start` + `bot/link/exchange`. THE SLICE THIS NEEDS (designed here, not yet built): (1) accept a BEARER bot credential on the challenge door, resolved through the existing `external::bot_for_token` + suspension check, with the bot id taken from the token rather than the path; (2) carry the platform identity (`platform`, `platform_user_id`) on the challenge row so a code is bound to the person it was minted for, and copy it onto the link row at confirmation — without it the bot cannot tell which Discord user a link belongs to, which is the entire question it is asking; (3) `GET /me/bots/{id}/links` (bearer) returning per-pseud links and their platform users, so the bot learns the outcome; (4) the reader still confirms on the site — the bot must never be able to confirm its own challenge, or 'what am I granting' becomes a page nobody reads. REMAINING BLOCKER beyond code: a Discord APPLICATION for darkhold itself (the host holds only ascend's identity; reusing it posts darkbot's replies as ascend) and a guild invite. Credential half only. | CODE HALF BUILT 2026-11-12 (step 4; the row still needs the credential): any bot credential now mints a challenge for a named platform user and reads back who linked. CENSUS: ADAPT — the three §23.2 doors existed, the principal did not. A bot registration's token carries acting_pseud_id NULL (0083), so RequireActor answered 403 at the mint door and resolve_bearer answered 401 before the handler could 404 a suspended bot; auth::BotCaller::{Session,Bot} + RequireBotOrOwner name the two callers instead of flattening them into one Actor, and bot_registration_for_token matches the registration's OWN token_id (not a linked reader's) and returns its state so the handler answers 404. Migration 0215 (both dialects) puts platform + platform_user_id on link_challenges; the reader still confirms on the site (a bot that could confirm its own challenge makes 'what am I granting' a page nobody reads); GET /me/bots/{id}/links returns per-pseud links with platform, platform_user, linked_at, and bot_name from api_tokens.name (bot_registrations has no name column). PostgreSQL needed ::text casts on both sides of uuid = text joins (api_tokens.id is UUID, token_id is TEXT).

open_requirements.requirement: dh audit --since 7d: the account owner sees every write their tokens made
open_requirements.notes: Power-user sweep P25. Automation is accountable to the person it acts for; the operation log already records the writes. | HALF-BUILT 2026-11-11 (server side done, verb not written, attribution impossible as the schema stands). SHIPPED: `GET /api/v1/me/audit-log` now takes `since` (RFC 3339) and `limit` (1..200, default 50) and echoes both back. Without a lower bound the route could only answer 'the newest fifty entries', which is not the question: a quiet account's week falls off the end of the page and a busy one's page covers an hour. The bound is NORMALISED to second precision with `identity::format_rfc3339` before it reaches SQL, because this schema stores `created_at` at second precision on purpose and a caller's `.500` fraction compares digit-by-digit back to front — so a fraction would silently exclude the entry it names. A bound that is not a timestamp is refused 422 naming the format it wants, rather than ignored, because ignoring it answers a different question than the one asked. TESTS: milestone_14 my_audit_log_takes_a_lower_bound_and_normalises_a_fraction_to_the_column 1/1 SQLite and 1/1 PostgreSQL — three entries at 2026-11-01/05/10, `since=11-05T00:00:00Z` returns [new, middle] and includes its own instant, `since=11-05T00:00:00.500Z` returns the same two and echoes `2026-11-05T00:00:00Z`, `limit=1` returns the newest, `since=7d` is 422. MUTANT: the comparison flipped to `<=` -> the list comes back as [middle, old]. MISSING, and why the row stays planned: (1) `dh audit --since 7d` — the CLI verb, which must resolve relative durations client-side and send RFC 3339 (deliberately not implemented yet, so the row is not claimed); (2) ATTRIBUTION: `audit_log` has no token id column, so the row's own words — 'every write their tokens made' — cannot be answered. `list_audit_log` scopes by `actor`, which is the human. Telling a reader 'your token did this' needs the write path to record which credential was used; until it does, the honest surface is 'what your account did', and the row's claim is only half met.

Per-surface strength via [taste] gravity_per_surface + gravity_ceiling (refused outside 0..=1 at load, and it bounds the number in force including the global value) + gravity_locked; TasteConfig::strength_for(surface). NOT DONE: story.similar / library.because_you_shelved and the other registry surfaces have no candidate pipeline to pull on, so discover.feed and the concierge (`home.curated`) honour the layer (1f05deff); taste_signal SHIPPED f74bd400: darkhold_db::taste_signal::for_account scores each candidate by the share of ITS canonical entities that appear on the works the account has shelved (share of the candidate, not of the shelf); absent from the map = unmeasured, Some(0.0) = measured and cold, None = no shelf at all; wired on both gravity surfaces. open_requirements.requirement: one shared taste crate and one JSON schema set, so darkhold and suki compute blend, affinity and the passport identically
open_requirements.notes: The synergy row, and the one that keeps the others honest: two products that each implement the blend will disagree within a month, and a passport whose semantics differ between sender and receiver is worse than none. A small Rust crate with no product dependencies plus versioned JSON schemas; both binaries depend on it, neither forks it. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.  | CENSUS 2026-11-11 (measured, no code written): REUSE the mechanism, BUILD the crate. (1) No shared taste crate exists: `ls ~/code-local/rust` has polaris-candidates and polaris-eval, no polaris-taste. (2) The duplication is real and counted: `rg -l -i 'fn blend|affinity'` over the estate gives darkhold 55 files, suki 38, ascend 7, whitebois 4, tessera 4, orbitals 4, commons 1. (3) darkhold already HAS a taste crate (crates/taste, 'the taste engine: the catalogue, the graph, the ranker and the budgets', binaries + lib) but it depends on `darkhold-domain` — so it cannot be the shared crate as it stands: extracting it means deciding which types move out of the product's domain first. That is the real work of this row, and it is a design decision, not a copy. (4) The estate ALREADY has the shared-crate pattern and uses it here: crates/taste depends on `polaris-eval` by relative path '../../../../polaris-eval', with a comment saying 'path dependency until the Forgejo registry answers' — so the publishing mechanism the row asks for is REUSE, and its precondition (a registry that answers) is the one thing this row does not control. DECISION (recorded, not yet implemented): the shared crate is `polaris-taste`, containing the pure parts of darkhold-taste that speak only in domain primitives (budget, diversify, ladder, embed) plus the affinity/blend math, with the product-shaped parts (catalogue, graph, collab, health — which read a table or a product's rows) staying in each product behind a trait the shared crate defines. The JSON schema set is versioned with the crate, and the passport schema is the one that must be identical on both sides because a passport whose semantics differ between sender and receiver is worse than none. NOT STARTED: no crate was created, because a crate nothing depends on is the 'component nobody calls' failure, and the first commit of an adoption row must be a dependency, not a `pub mod`. NEXT STEP: split the domain dependency, then move budget/diversify/ladder/embed, then make darkhold depend on it and delete its copies (adoption proved by deletion), then suki.

open_requirements.requirement: Every db listing query that a reader surface depends on is either wired to a route or deleted: no function exists only to satisfy its own test.
open_requirements.notes: ORPHAN RATCHET over crates/db: every pass deletes or wires one dead store function, writes the failing test first, proves it with a mutant reverted from /tmp, and runs both engines. Baseline 181 reachable-by-nothing queries at the start of the ratchet (43 -> 57 when reachability was corrected to be module-qualified; the header of docs/plans/orphan-queries.txt records why), now 36. VERBATIM PASS JOURNAL: docs/plans/m70-13-pass-log.md (one section per pass, with the defect measured, the decision and its rejected alternative, the mutant that reddened, and the deploy record). The cell below keeps the latest passes and the standing rules; the journal keeps everything. STANDING RULES LEARNED (each cost a pass): a function whose only caller is a test, or nobody, and which is a narrower/less-safe twin of the product path, is deleted and the test redirected to the real entry point. A rendered route is the only proof of a feature; a component with tests is not. Refusal shapes are features: 404 not 403 to a stranger, tombstone not 404 for a deleted comment, 422 naming the field rather than 500. A producer that writes a derived row must write it in the same statement as the fact, or the fact and its derivation diverge. A reader whose writer does not exist reports zero and means nothing: measure the table before believing the panel. Config switches must have readers; registries must be listable and writable; and a rule stated in prose needs its machine-readable half in the same commit (taste_notifications said off-by-default and was missing from OPT_IN). LATEST PASSES: 73 conversation privacy guards; 74 tag confirmation door; 75 record_view writes kind+source; 76 entity parentage + children expansion; 77 warmth producer (kudos, comments); 78 FinishWork on the transition; 79 deleted the unfiltered notification twins; 80 quality-signal operator door; 81 reader_positivity derived from visible reviews; 82 a verdict about the work is not praise (generic dislike held, not counted). DEPLOY RECORD: passes are batched or deployed individually with a named pg_dump verified by `pg_restore -l | grep -c 'TABLE DATA'` (392 tables), a release build, `migrate` from the tree, and a live probe. Latest: 2026-11-10 04:12, build 0.1.0+a1bb450a. PASS 83 (done) 2026-11-10: ReadUnit, the last of 41.2's four acts. Near-miss first: I wrote a migration for a new reader_unit_reads table, then found reading_unit_read already exists - keyed on the PSEUD, written on the first OPEN, consumed by the chapters/words reading goals. Two facts: reading_unit_read (pseud, first open, goals) vs reader_unit_completions (account, first COMPLETION, warmth). open_requirements.requirement: Browse, search, library and the overflow view of every recommendation rail render results as dense list rows — title, author, provenance word, word count, unit count, completion, rating, date, metrics — with a stated total and cursor pagination, never a card grid and never infinite scroll.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 2, no new backend. 141,317 catalogue rows behind a card grid is the strongest finding in the external design and the cheapest. Sorts stay the closed vocabulary; sort changes order and never hides results (§8.1). Row height consistent; quick actions on hover/focus, always visible on mobile.

open_requirements.requirement: The operator console becomes its own visual register: dense rows, monospace values, red/amber/green status with a word, an alert bar naming every red state with a 'fix' link, 404 for non-operators, and no component shared with the reader-facing site that would soften a failure.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 3. §8.20 made operational: the console is allowed to be less beautiful than the reader and is not allowed to hide a red state. Today the ~30 admin surfaces use the same component library as the reading site. Acceptance: the admin overview renders each group from live counts and every warning has an action; a non-operator gets 404.

open_requirements.requirement: The reader gains an auto-hiding bar (back, unit navigation, position, typography, bookmark, in-work search) and a typography panel whose settings are per reader and per work, with provenance shown ('your default' / 'instance default' / 'this work') and a reset at each level.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 2, additive to the existing server-rendered reader. Typography must stay independent of the site theme (§4.11 of the proposal); the panel offers font family including a dyslexia-friendly option, size, line height, measure in characters, justification and four functional presets. Acceptance: settings survive a device change; an RTL work and an LTR work do not share them; the panel renders without JS as a form.

open_requirements.requirement: Reader position is honest: a position recorded against an older revision is reported as stale and offered as a choice, two devices that disagree are offered as a choice, and a position with no reliable evidence renders '—' rather than a false 0%.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 3. The anchor system exists; the honesty layer does not. §8.14 and §8.17 make silence and silent overwrite both bugs; §11 forbids fake precision. Acceptance: three tests, one per state, each asserting the choice text and that no percentage is fabricated. f3aca3fc: domain::reading::ResumeState has four states — current / stale / unmeasured / conflict — each with its own sentence, and percent() is Option<u16> so only `current` carries a number; display() renders '—' otherwise, which is what makes 'no measurement' unable to become '0%' in a template. AGREEMENT_PERMILLE = 50: a slider moved a pixel is not a second opinion. A recorded revision whose unit is gone is stale with current: None (an anchor cannot be honoured), not current. db::reading::positions_with_current_revision joins each stored row to the revision its unit points at NOW in one statement, so the answer is about one moment; GET /api/v1/reading/progress publishes `resume: {state, percent, display, sentence, needs_a_choice}` beside the existing positions/resolution, and the raw rows still travel so a page can offer the stale place as a choice. The deeper bug fixed on the way: save_progress recorded the revision ONLY when the client sent content_revision, so a browser that omits it owned a position that could never be detected as stale — it now resolves the unit's current revision server-side when the client is silent, while still recording an older client-sent revision as the real stale case. STILL MISSING: the reader's bar and the choice UI; the API states all three cases.

open_requirements.requirement: Facet counts are a server capability with a latency budget: one endpoint returns counts per facet value under the current filter set, the UI renders them per group and shows '—' while they update, and the p95 stays inside the budget on the 141k-row catalogue.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 3, and the most underpriced item in the external design: no route in the 720 returned a facet count — STALE: /api/v1/facets has returned counts per facet value since M64-10 (one scan, four facets, when_unknown), and /api/v1/facets/words since M71-12 (grep '"facets"' crates/app/src is empty). This is an aggregate query plan — indexes, a cache, a budget — not a component. Acceptance: a load measurement with the decision rule fixed before the run, documented in the row. Remaining work is therefore the UI half (per-group counts, the '—' pending state) and the p95 measurement on the 141k catalogue with the decision rule fixed before the run; the aggregate endpoint itself is not the gap. DECISION RULE, fixed 2026-11-07 before any run (recorded in advance so it cannot be chosen after the numbers): target GET /api/v1/facets with no filters — the four-facet aggregate — against the live darkhold catalogue on thinkcentre (58,042 works, 141,317 library_items, 30,982 work_tags), requested 50 times sequentially from the host over 127.0.0.1:8081 after 5 warm requests, one token cookie, no other load. PASS iff p50 <= 100 ms AND p95 <= 200 ms AND every response is 200 with four facet groups; FAIL otherwise, in which case the measured numbers go in this row and the next step is indexes/caching, not a re-run with a looser bar. 41e847e4 MEASURED, rule pre-registered at 82db6c0e before any run: 50 sequential requests after 5 warmups on the live catalogue (58,042 works / 141,317 library_items) -> 50/50 200 but p50 297 ms, p95 372 ms against a budget of p50<=100 / p95<=200 = FAIL. EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) ruled out the index answer: three sequential scans (works 58,042; units 127,474; revisions 127,474) + a 12.5 MB external-merge sort for one group aggregate, 235 ms before the sort and 398 ms total — facets are O(catalogue) by construction. Fix: crates/app/src/facets_cache.rs memoises the answer per (database, filter set) for 60 s, bounded at 256 entries with TTL eviction; both facet-bearing endpoints publish computed_at_ms_ago and the facet door publishes cache_ttl_seconds, so the staleness bound is part of the contract rather than a hidden property. The database is part of the key because a filter string alone does not say whose catalogue it counts — a test process opening one database per test served one test's counts to another and went red on exactly that. clear() exists for an operator action that must see its own write. RE-MEASURED after deploy: warm p50 2.83 ms / p95 6.05 ms / max 7.36 ms over the same 50-request sequence; the pre-registered rule as written PASSES on that sequence, and the honest reading is that the sequence is warm — the cold path is stated separately (1,174 ms first request after restart, ~300 ms steady-state scan), not averaged in. ALONG THE WAY, two production-breaking defects in the same scan, invisible to the SQLite-only tests: (1) SUM(bigint) is NUMERIC on PostgreSQL so `GET /api/v1/facets` answered every live request 500 with `mismatched types ... SQL type NUMERIC` — fixed with a per-backend ::BIGINT cast, guarded by crates/db/tests/facets_two_engines.rs; (2) the scan built `?1`,`?2` placeholders and handed the raw text to sqlx on both engines, so EVERY FILTERED facet request failed with `operator does not exist: ? integer` on PostgreSQL — the statement now goes through Database::sql and uses bare `?` (with `?1` the rewrite produced `$11`), with CAST(? AS BIGINT) so the window bound has a type. STILL MISSING: the UI half — per-group rendering and the '—' pending state while counts update.

open_requirements.requirement: The word-count filter is a real histogram: a distribution endpoint returns ten buckets for the current filter set, the control draws them and lets a range be selected over the bars, and the selected bounds are stated as numbers.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 4, depends on M71-11's aggregate surface — same query shape, different grouping. Decorative bars fed by invented data are forbidden (the proposal is right that the histogram must be real). 9fd5955a: the distribution endpoint exists — GET /api/v1/facets/words?tag=&q=&buckets=&min_words=&max_words=&max_rating= returns 10 population-equal buckets (quantile edges, not equal width: equal width puts 8 of 10 skewed works in one bar) with low/high/count/share, plus measured/unknown/total/when_unknown over the same filtered set the facet route describes. Unmeasured rows (a unit with no current revision — this schema has revisions.word_count NOT NULL, so that IS the unmeasured state) are excluded from every bucket and counted in unknown; buckets partition the measured set exactly once, ties included; empty buckets are dropped and the rest renumbered so a chart has no gaps. STILL MISSING for the row: the control that draws the bars and lets a range be selected over them, and M71-11's latency measurement.

open_requirements.requirement: Every surface that enumerates a partially covered dimension states its coverage: the fandom facet leads with 'N of M works are tagged (P%)', fandom and source pages split hosted from referenced, and the numbers come from one aggregate view rather than being typed into copy.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 3. 5.4% fandom coverage is a fact the CLI already prints and the UI hides; a catalogue that hides it is claiming a completeness it does not have. Acceptance: the numbers on a page equal a query's output, asserted in a test. bf404997: db::taxonomy::dimension_coverage(dimension, value) computes the view count and the published+public catalogue count in ONE statement (two round trips could report a share of two different archives) and builds the sentence there, so no two surfaces phrase the same gap differently. Three cases: works>0 → '2 of 5 works in this archive are tagged slow burn (40.0%)'; works==0 with a non-empty catalogue → 'No published work in this archive is tagged X any more' (a dimension page exists because something carried it, so zero means the rows went away; 0.0% is true and useless); empty catalogue → 'nothing to measure against'. Wired on /api/v1/tags/{tag} and /api/v1/fandoms/{fandom} as `coverage` + on the DOCUMENT tag page (its bare '12 works' replaced), because the document is the surface a crawler and a JS-off reader sees. STILL MISSING: the facet panel's 'N of M works are tagged (P%)' leading line is a UI claim (the API already publishes known/unknown/total per facet). a7664d54 closes the collection half differently from the tag/fandom half, on purpose: a collection is a hand-picked set, so events::collection_coverage counts entries vs readable entries INSIDE it (published+public+undeleted) instead of against the archive, publishes hidden as its own number, and has three sentences — '2 of 5 entries are readable; 3 entries are private, unpublished or deleted.', '2 entries, all of them readable.', 'This collection has no entries yet.' The remaining M71-13 item is the facet panel's leading 'N of M works are tagged (P%)' line, which is a UI claim: the API already publishes known/unknown/total per facet and coverage on tag, fandom and collection. | MEASURED 2026-11-11: the share clause is BUILT AND TESTED — db::taxonomy::dimension_coverage (one statement) emitted by /tags/{tag} and the fandom page, with crates/app/tests/m71_13_coverage.rs 2/2 (API sentence, document page, drafts/private/deleted excluded, zero case) and tag_page.rs asserting '2 of N works in this archive are tagged'. REMAINING, one clause: 'fandom and source pages split hosted from referenced' — Coverage has no hosted/referenced pair and no schema column distinguishes a hosted work from one this instance only references, so the split needs the origin concept first; adding two numbers now would be lifecycle=published under two names.

open_requirements.requirement: Settings show inheritance with provenance at every level (instance, account, pseud, per-work), deep-link to the exact control, offer a reset at each level that overrides, and reflect inline changes made elsewhere with a 'set as default' affordance.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 4. The product already has per-work reader overrides and content filters enforced server-side; the settings surface does not explain where a value came from, so an override looks like a bug. Locked chips for server-enforced filters carry a link to settings and no dismiss control (§8.16). b799f828: GET /api/v1/settings/privacy now carries `provenance` (account keys) and `pseud_provenance` (per pseud), each {value, source: SettingSource (instance|account|pseud), reset: {method, path, becomes} | null, note?}; source reuses darkhold_domain::settings::SettingSource so /settings/export and this door cannot spell a level differently. New door DELETE /api/v1/settings/privacy/{key}[?pseud_id=] clears one level (204 whether or not a row existed; 422 on an unknown key; 404 on a pseud that is not yours — deliberately not 403, which would be an account-enumeration oracle). THE FINDING: registration and pseud creation write every key at account/pseud scope by design, and those rows were indistinguishable from choices, so a fresh account reported six settings as its own decisions and a later instance-default change could never reach it — migration 0180 adds privacy_settings.origin ('onboarding'|'reader', default 'reader' so pre-existing rows keep their meaning rather than being relabelled by a guess); onboarding writes 'onboarding', every reader write writes 'reader', and an onboarding row is reported as instance with a note and no reset. This reverses the earlier in-code claim that the difference 'is not actionable'. STILL MISSING: the per-work level, the deep link to the exact control, and typography/gravity settings are not yet reported through this vocabulary.

open_requirements.requirement: The query string and the facet panel are one state: every facet is expressible in the grammar, or it is rendered as a visible chip that cannot be dropped by editing the string — no filter may disappear because it had no field.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 3. The query grammar has no fields for provenance, source or language; a design that presents the string as the state would silently drop those filters, which is hidden state the product forbids (§8.2 closed vocabulary, §8.14 named degradation). 6c35aee9: the ledger's premise was wrong about which facet was missing. Language has a field; the RATING CEILING did not, and it is the one filter every search page has — the route applied max_rating while the grammar could not spell it, so editing the string dropped the filter from view with the filter still in force. Fix: ValueKind::Rank + QueryField::Rating comparable, RATING_RANKS (general<teen<mature<explicit) in query.rs read by both parser validation and the renderer's CASE (text comparison would order by spelling, not by the product's judgement); unknown names refused with the vocabulary listed. New crates/domain/src/filter_state.rs: FilterState{text,min_words,max_words,max_rating,sort,pinned} with canonical query_string() (no `sort:` — writing a field the parser does not know produces a string that no longer parses), chips() where expressible parts are editable_in_query+removable and pinned parts are neither and carry the reason, unexpressed_note() naming them in words, and from_query_string() so a client does not reimplement the grammar. GET /api/v1/search now returns state{query,chips,unexpressed_note} beside filters and facets, with the reader's content filters as pinned chips (kind = the filter's own type). Also removed ideas rows M63-37/M63-38 from crates/domain/src/modules/ideas.rs and docs/ideas-catalogue.json — both had become implemented-locally-tested and the idea-catalogue test was red; scripts/ideas_catalogue.py refuses to run here because two vault source files are absent, so the removal was by hand to match its output. STILL MISSING: the panel that renders the chips is UI; provenance/source filters have no route, so when they exist they join `pinned` with their own reason.

open_requirements.requirement: The remaining document-class pages migrate in ADR 0006's order - work page /works/{id}, fandom and tag pages, search results, author and collection/series pages - each shipped as server-rendered HTML whose content, links and primary action work with no script, with its Svelte route deleted in the same commit and a server test asserting the no-JS content.
open_requirements.notes: Opened by M71-01 (8a51f9de), which shipped the landing page. Order and reasons are in docs/adr/0006-one-binary-two-renderers.md. The work page is next and is the one that matters for link previews and crawlers: it needs the public view (works::public_view) plus a session-aware split, because the SPA work page carries the signed-in actions (bookmark, kudos, author tools) - a signed-in reader keeps the application, an anonymous one gets the document. Acceptance per page: a test that fetches the HTML, parses it and asserts the content with no script execution, plus a live probe; the Svelte route is removed in the same commit so the count only goes down. PROGRESS 50635a36: landing page (8a51f9de) and work page /works/{id} shipped as documents, each with a no-script test and a live probe. The work page uses reading_decision_publishing_metadata, answers every denial with one 404 page (bodies compared byte for byte in the test), shows a restricted work's record and withholds its text, and hands a signed-in reader the application per ADR 0006. REMAINING per ADR 0006's order: fandom and tag pages, search results, author page, collection and series pages - each deletes its Svelte route in the same commit. TAG PAGE ed9c7088: GET /tags/{tag} is a document listing the works behind a tag (query filters published public works; empty tag = 404 page; capped at 50 with 'more than 50' rather than a false total). The document shell moved to routes/document.rs at the third caller and work_page's copy was deleted. REMAINING: search results, author page, collection and series pages; then delete the Svelte routes for the pages already served as documents.

open_requirements.requirement: `polaris-affinity` 0.1: one crate owning profile→score arithmetic — set/count similarity, weighted mean over present evidence, confidence blending `n/(n+k)`, bounded multiplier, percentile within a cohort, age decay — pure functions with no state, no DB and no `product` parameter.

darkhold adopts `polaris-affinity` by deletion: `domain/affinity.rs` keeps only the adapter that builds `Component`s, its arithmetic moves to the crate, and its existing tests run as the crate's test vectors.

ascend adopts `polaris-affinity` by deletion: `themes.rs::{confidence, combine, multiplier, percentile_ranks}` are removed in favour of the crate, with `MIN_MULTIPLIER`/`MAX_MULTIPLIER`/`CONFIDENCE_PRIOR` remaining ascend's declared data.

orbital adopts `polaris-affinity` by deletion: `ranking.rs::{cosine, tag_relevance}` are removed in favour of the crate, and the `0.0`-for-unknown ambiguity becomes an explicit `None` whose meaning is decided by each surface.

Seed the instance from the operator's rated reading list, through the product's own write path: measure first, prove the write path, then a dry-run seeder, then apply through the service, then rebuild what the ratings feed. The list is a prior, not a population, and the plan says so.
open_requirements.notes: Registered 2026-11-12 because the repository held a dated roadmap that this ledger did not: the idea catalogue's coverage gate refused to regenerate until every idea a live roadmap names had a home, and the honest home for a proposal is a row, not an exemption. Measured basis (taste_census.py, 2026-11-11): accounts 20, taste_profiles 2, instance_theme 1, rating 0, work_ratings 0, work_taste_vectors 0 — twenty accounts and not one rating, so every ranking surface on the busiest member is decoration. Phases: 0 measure, 1 the write path (estate ledger 406, a prerequisite), 2 the seeder with a dry run first, 3 apply through the service, 4 rebuild the taste vectors and the instance theme, 5 the verification that closes it. Non-goal stated in the document: this is one person's list and may not be presented as a population.
